What is alpha-thalassemia?(A genetic problem with producing red blood cells that ranges from completely asymptomatic, like your baby, to severe life threatening anemia, which your baby does not have.)

Will he have any medical problems as a result of this? (Probably not. He may have mild anemia with small red blood cells, depending on the results of testing that cannot be done until he is 9-12 months old. If he has mild anemia, the most important thing is for him to tell his doctor that he has a form of alpha thalassemia to avoid unnecessary iron dosing for presumed iron deficiency anemia)

Babies make a certain kind of hemoglobin when they are inside the mother that changes over to normal adult hemoglobin during the first year of life, then stays the same for the rest of their life. We have to wait for Micah’s bone marrow to complete this change over to the adult pattern to see which form of alpha thalassemia he may have.
